Messages.Author: MSummers
Messages.Body:
If Karsh ADV is unmerged, and has been named Imperator from the political action, does he have 3 votes for his title and 6 additional votes in a blood hunt referendum? For a total of 9 during a blood hunt referendum?

If so, what happens when unmerged ADV Imperator Karsh becomes merged? Does he go down to 6 votes?

It seems to me that Karsh merging while already being Imperator from the card, would lose the card title, and gain the imperator from his merged text. Therefore he would lose the additional 3 blood hunt votes from the card title, as Karsh's merged Imperator title does not state that he gets the extra 3 blood hunt votes from the title.

If that is the case, would an already merged Karsh becoming Imperator via political action, get 3 votes (Imperator) 3 Blood hunt votes (Imperator) and 3 Blood hunt votes (Karsh ADV text)?

Overall I am looking for a merged Karsh with 9 votes during a blood hunt, and I would like to know if the order matters.

Gangrel

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
> Pascal wrote:
> 3+3+3 is 9, so advanced (or merged) Karsh with an Imperator would indeed have 9 votes in a blood hunt referendum.
>
Wait let me get this straight;

Advanced Karsh with an Imperator political card on him, during a blood hunt gets:

Imperator Unique Title: 3 votes
Imperator special card text: 3 votes
Karsh Advanced special card text: 3 votes

3+3+3 = 9 votes. That seems somewhat obvious.

Then you merge Karsh, giving him the unique title of Imperator. To receive a title, you first have to give up any titles you have; in this case the Imperator title from the card on him. However, I don't believe you need to actually burn the card too. So then we get:

Imperator Title (from Karsh): 3 votes
Special Text from the Imperator political card (since that stays and merely says "this vampire" anyway): 3 votes
Karsh advanced special text: 3 votes

Of course, when you actually have to burn the card you should lose the 3 votes from the political card.

This could lead to interesting scenarios. For example, I have a vampire with the Imperator title (6 votes in bloodhunts), which gets contested. I give up the title, but the card technically stays so I get to keep my 3 additional votes in bloodhunts. I suppose somewhat similar to how Gratiano's cardtext works.

amirite?

Messages.Author: salem

Nope. These days the title-granting cards have all been rewritten so that the title IS the card. So if you lose the title, you lose the card.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
If you have Unmerged Karsh, give him the Imperator Vote Title and then Merge Karsh you will lose the Imperator Vote Card since he will gain the new title Imperator from merging which will replace his previous title of Imperator Vote Card. This gives him 6 votes in a Bloodhunt referendum.

If you have Merged Karsh and give him the Imperator Vote Title, Karsh would lose his Merged Imperator and gain Imperator Vote Title which results in him having 9 votes in a Bloodhunt Referendum.

All of this assuming that when you gain a title you already have, that you lose the previous title. E.g. Justicar to Prince = lose old, gain new. Prince of Berlin to Prince of Berlin = lose old Prince of Berlin to gain new Prince of Berlin.

Messages.Author: cauecoraini
Messages.Body:
if he has a card "placeholder" that grants him the title and he gets another one, the card is burned, (so no +3 votes from cardtext)and if he has a title (by minion cardtext) already and gains a card "placeholder" for a title, he forfeits his (minion cardtext) title and receive the one in the card. But his minion cardtext still aplies, so +3 from himself and +3 from imperator card, only if he was already an Imperator and then gained the card.

The problem here is that the card "placeholder" for a title is burned if the minion having it gains another title, but his (minion) own cardtext is not erased by the Imperator card placeholder.

By the way his +3 votes on blood hunts is not attached to his title as is on the Imperator Card.
